MAIN ANALYSIS COMPLETE (executed analysis.py on data/nls_raw.csv, 12,686 respondents).

## Primary result — Median family net wealth (nominal $), non-missing values
| Year | Group | n | Median |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1985 | Black | 1,699 | $1,600 |
| 1985 | Hispanic | 2,631 | $500 |
| 1985 | White-proxy (non-Black/non-Hispanic) | 5,774 | $3,500 |
| 1990 | Black | 1,528 | $4,800 |
| 1990 | Hispanic | 2,431 | $1,600 |
| 1990 | White-proxy | 5,336 | $12,972 |
| 1996 | Black | 1,368 | $9,800 |
| 1996 | Hispanic | 2,114 | $2,562 |
| 1996 | White-proxy | 3,557 | $42,600 |

## Median ratios (White-proxy / Black, White-proxy / Hispanic)
| Year | White/Black | White/Hispanic |
|---|---|---|
| 1985 | 2.19× | 7.00× |
| 1990 | 2.70× | 8.11× |
| 1996 | 4.35× | 16.62× |

## Robustness — 90th percentile (nominal $)
| Year | Black | Hispanic | White-proxy |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1985 | 18,397 | 9,200 | 32,285 |
| 1990 | 64,030 | 26,200 | 110,922 |
| 1996 | 117,000 | 56,000 | 245,900 |
Same ordering (white > black > hispanic); the upper-tail gap is even larger.

## Robustness — Median after dropping top-coded repeated value (1990: 1,321,099; 1996: 1,232,183)
| Year | Black | Hispanic | White-proxy | (dropped in white-proxy) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1985 | 1,600 | 500 | 3,500 | 0 |
| 1990 | 4,700 | 1,600 | 12,500 | 70 |
| 1996 | 9,500 | 2,500 | 40,500 | 124 |
Medians shift by <5% — the top-coded extremes do not drive the result.

## Sensitivity — Per-capita median (family net wealth / Family size, 1979)
| Year | Black | Hispanic | White-proxy |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1985 | 325 | 95 | 900 |
| 1990 | 1,000 | 329 | 3,400 |
| 1996 | 2,183 | 506 | 10,700 |
Ordering preserved per-capita.

## Missingness / attrition by group and year
| Year | Black | Hispanic | White-proxy |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1985 | 15.1% | 17.1% | 23.1% |
| 1990 | 23.7% | 23.4% | 28.9% |
| 1996 | 31.7% | 33.4% | 52.6% |

## HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded)
From 1985 onward, the median family net wealth of the white (non-Black/non-Hispanic) cohort is consistently and substantially higher than that of the black and Hispanic cohorts, and the racial wealth gap widens over time. In 1985 the white-proxy median ($3,500) was about 2.2× the black median ($1,600) and 7.0× the Hispanic median ($500); by 1990 it had risen to $12,972 (2.7× black, 8.1× Hispanic); and by 1996 to $42,600 (4.4× black, 16.6× Hispanic). The black cohort sits above the Hispanic cohort in every year. This white > black > hispanic ordering is robust to using the 90th percentile, to dropping the top-coded repeated values, and to expressing wealth per household member.

Caveats that keep the claim data-grounded: (1) "white" is a non-Black/non-Hispanic proxy (code 3), not strictly non-Hispanic white — it also includes Asian, Native American, and multiracial respondents; (2) wealth is family/household-level, not individual-level (each respondent carries their family's net wealth); (3) figures are nominal — not inflation-adjusted and not per-capita in the primary estimate — so part of the cross-year "widening" reflects inflation rather than pure real growth; and (4) the 1996 estimates rest on a heavily attrited sample (~45% missing overall; 52.6% missing for the white-proxy group), so that year's figures are the least secure.

payload.workflow: Loaded data/nls_raw.csv (12,686x61). For each year in {1985,1990,1996} and each racial/ethnic group {1=Black, 2=Hispanic, 3=White-proxy}, computed the median of family net wealth over non-missing values (listwise exclusion), reporting per-group n. Computed white/black and white/hispanic median ratios. Robustness: (a) 90th percentile per group/year; (b) median recomputed after dropping the top-coded repeated values (1,321,099 in 1990; 1,232,183 in 1996); (c) per-capita sensitivity (family net wealth / Family size, 1979). Also tabulated missingness/attrition by group and year. All checks preserve the white > black > hispanic ordering.
